opencode-agent-runtime

Track total agent running time per session and per project in OpenCode V2.
Live current-run timer + persisted session/project totals, including subagents.

## What it tracks | Scope | Meaning | | --- | --- | | **Session** | Completed plus currently running agent execution time for the selected session **and all of its subagent descendants**. | | **Project** | Total across every session in the project, including subagents. | | **Current timer** | Live clock for the active execution in the selected session family. | | **Persistent** | Completed totals and the running-timer start are stored in OpenCode's plugin storage and survive reloads/restarts. | Time is measured as wall-clock time between `session.execution.started` and `session.execution.succeeded` / `failed` / `interrupted`. This includes waiting for tools, permission prompts, and subagents. In other words: the time the agent is actually busy, not just raw model time. ## Install ```bash git clone https://github.com/officialPlocki/opencode-agent-runtime.git \ ~/.local/share/opencode-agent-runtime-src cd ~/.local/share/opencode-agent-runtime-src npm install --omit=dev ``` Add it to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (global, for every project) or to `opencode.json` / `.opencode/opencode.json` in a project: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": [ "/home/you/.local/share/opencode-agent-runtime-src" ] } ``` Then run `/reload` in OpenCode. No restart is required. ### Versioned local install The repository also ships an `install:local` helper that copies the current version into `~/.local/share/opencode-agent-runtime/` and installs its production dependencies: ```bash npm run install:local ``` Point the plugin entry at the printed directory. ### Options ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "/home/you/.local/share/opencode-agent-runtime/0.2.1", "options": { "hideWhenIdle": false } } ] } ``` | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `hideWhenIdle` | `false` | Hide the sidebar panel while the session has never run and is not currently running. | ## Usage ### Sidebar ```text AGENT RUNTIME now 2m 11s session 1h 23m 4 runs · 2 subagents project 12h 45m 38 runs · 7 sessions 2 running ``` `now` is the live timer for the active execution in the current session family. It keeps ticking while the selected session or one of its subagents is running. `session` includes completed time plus the live portion of every running execution in that family. ### Slash command ```text /agent-runtime ``` Posts a short summary as a synthetic message into the current session. ### Tool The `agent_runtime` tool returns the same summary so an agent can query it directly. ## How it works - The server part subscribes to OpenCode's execution events. - On startup it reconciles running sessions with the server. An execution that is already in progress is adopted automatically, so the live timer resumes from its persisted start time instead of resetting to zero. - Finished executions are saved immediately. While an execution is running, a heartbeat writes the last known state every 15 seconds. - If the server dies mid-run, the execution is counted up to the last heartbeat and marked as `interrupted` on the next start. - Tracking starts when the plugin first loads. Earlier executions are not reconstructed retroactively. - A session total includes its own executions plus every descendant subagent session. The project total independently sums every session in the project, so subagent time is counted once in the project and once in its ancestor session total. - Parent and subagent sessions can run at the same time. The totals are therefore additive agent runtime, not the project's wall-clock time. - Storage is isolated per project (`state/`). ### Timer persistence The running timer is not just a TUI-local counter. The server stores the execution's `startedAt` in the plugin state as soon as it starts, and the 15-second heartbeat saves the last known state while it runs. After a plugin reload or server restart, the plugin reconciles against the active session list and restores the timer from its original start time. If the session is no longer running, the execution is closed at the last known end (or heartbeat) instead of leaving a stuck timer. ## Development ```bash npm install npm run typecheck npm test ``` The state and formatting logic lives in `src/runtime.ts` and has no OpenCode dependencies, so it can be tested in isolation. ## Limitations - Only executions that happen after install / plugin load are counted. - A hard crash can lose at most the last heartbeat interval of a running timer. - Because session totals add subagent time on top of the parent's own busy time, concurrent parent/subagent work is counted as agent runtime, not wall-clock. - If the same project runs in multiple OpenCode instances with this plugin at the same time, they share the same storage key. For normal single-machine use this is not a problem. - Stats contain session IDs and titles; they stay in OpenCode's local plugin storage and are not sent anywhere. ## License MIT

# Security policy

## Supported versions

The current `0.1.x` line receives fixes.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report security issues privately through a GitHub security advisory on the
repository. Do not open a public issue for credential leaks or data exposure.

## Data handling

- The plugin stores runtime statistics in OpenCode's local plugin storage.
- Stored records contain session IDs, optional session titles, parent session
  IDs, timestamps, and durations.
- The plugin makes no network requests and has no analytics or telemetry.
- Statistics are exposed locally through the plugin RPC and the
  `agent_runtime` tool.
